addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- project-structure-validator: Validates project structure against co-location and architecture patterns defined in AGENTS.md (Tools: All tools)

- sol: General-purpose subagent running on Codex GPT-5.6 Sol via the claude-all gateway. Use for heavy implementation, deep debugging, second-opinion reviews, or any Task the orchestrator wants executed by GPT-5.6 Sol instead of a Claude model. Accepts any prompt a general-purpose agent would. (Tools: All tools)
- spark: General-purpose subagent running on Codex GPT-5.3 Spark (fast) via the claude-all gateway. Use for quick mechanical subtasks, bulk edits, and speed-over-depth work. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- understand-anything:architecture-analyzer: Analyzes a codebase's file structure, summaries, and import relationships to identify
logical architectural layers and assign every file to exactly one layer. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:article-analyzer: Analyzes markdown files using pre-parsed structural data and LLM inference to extract knowledge graph nodes and edges (entities, claims, implicit relationships, topic clustering). (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:assemble-reviewer: Reviews the output of merge-batch-graphs.py for semantic issues the script
cannot catch. Recovers dropped nodes/edges and fills cross-batch gaps. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:domain-analyzer: Analyzes codebases to extract business domain knowledge — domains, business flows, and process steps. Produces a domain-graph.json that maps how business logic flows through the code. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:file-analyzer: Analyzes batches of source files to produce knowledge graph nodes and edges.
Extracts file structure, functions, classes, and relationships using a two-phase
approach: structural extraction script followed by LLM semantic analysis. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:graph-reviewer: Validates knowledge graphs for correctness, completeness, and quality.
Runs systematic checks and renders approval or rejection decisions. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:knowledge-graph-guide: Use this agent when users need help understanding, querying, or working
with an Understand-Anything knowledge graph. Guides users through graph
structure, node/edge relationships, layer architecture, tours, and
dashboard usage. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:project-scanner: Scans a codebase directory to produce a structured inventory of all project files,
detected languages, frameworks, import maps, and estimated complexity. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:tour-builder: Designs guided learning tours through codebases, creating 5-15 pedagogical steps
that teach project architecture and key concepts in logical order. (Tools: All tools)

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\khair\.claude\skills\call-another-llm

<purpose>
Send a prompt to another LLM agent and get its response saved to a file.
Two separate scripts, one per LLM. Each runs the CLI in non-interactive mode and writes the raw response to tmp/llm-responses/.
</purpose>

<constraints>
- Each script runs the target LLM in non-interactive mode with auto-approve. Codex specifically runs in YOLO mode (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`): unsandboxed with full filesystem/network access, so it can implement changes, run tests, and reach the TEST database.
- Fail fast if the target CLI is not installed or returns a non-zero exit code.
- Output files contain only the raw response — no metadata.
- All output goes to `tmp/llm-responses/` with the pattern `<llm>-<label>-<timestamp>.md`.
</constraints>

<scripts>
- `scripts/call_codex.py` — calls Codex CLI
- `scripts/call_claude.py` — calls Claude Code CLI
</scripts>

<inputs>

**All scripts share:**
  - positional: `prompt` (required, except when using `--list-models`)
  - `--label`: optional label for the output filename (default: llm name)

**Codex-specific flags (`call_codex.py`):**
  - `-m` / `--model`: model to use (known model: `gpt-5.6-sol`; any string accepted)
  - `--effort`: reasoning effort level — `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `ultra` (`ultra` is heavy on usage but most capable)
  - `--list-models`: print known models, the current default, and valid effort levels, then exit

When `--model` is omitted, Codex uses the default from `~/.codex/config.toml`.
When `--effort` is omitted, Codex uses the effort configured in `config.toml` (default: `high`).
</inputs>

<workflow>
1. If the user has not specified which LLM to call, use the AskUser tool with options (Codex, Claude) to let the user choose. If the user wants both, confirm that before running two parallel calls.
2. Write the prompt to a file first (see prompt-file-methodology below).
3. Run the chosen script(s) passing the file contents: `"$(cat tmp/llm-prompts/{filename})"`.
4. Read the output file path from stdout (OUTPUT_FILE=...).
5. Read the response file to use the result.
</workflow>

<prompt-file-methodology>
Always write prompts to a file before passing to CLI scripts. This makes prompts reviewable,
debuggable, and preservable as an audit trail.

**Directory:** `tmp/llm-prompts/` (create with `mkdir -p` if it doesn't exist)

**File naming:** `{agentname}_{3 random lowercase letters}_{unix timestamp}.txt`
- `agentname` = the agent role or label (e.g. `codex-reviewer`, `claude-summarizer`)
- 3 random lowercase letters for uniqueness
- Unix timestamp in seconds
- Example: `codex-reviewer_xfm_1743926400.txt`

**Steps:**
1. `mkdir -p tmp/llm-prompts`
2. Generate filename: `{agentname}_$(cat /dev/urandom | tr -dc 'a-z' | head -c3)_$(date +%s).txt`
3. Write the full prompt to that file.
4. Pass to CLI: `uv run .../call_codex.py --label "..." "$(cat tmp/llm-prompts/{filename})"`
</prompt-file-methodology>

<examples>
```bash
# List available Codex models and effort levels
uv run "C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/mk-skills/call-another-llm/scripts/call_codex.py" --list-models

# Codex with default model and effort
uv run "C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/mk-skills/call-another-llm/scripts/call_codex.py" "Explain the trade-offs of this approach" --label "review"

# Codex with specific model and effort
uv run "C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/mk-skills/call-another-llm/scripts/call_codex.py" "Review this code" -m gpt-5.6-sol --effort high --label "review"
uv run "C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/mk-skills/call-another-llm/scripts/call_codex.py" "Deep analysis of this architecture" -m gpt-5.6-sol --effort ultra --label "deep-review"

# Claude
uv run "C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/mk-skills/call-another-llm/scripts/call_claude.py" "Summarise this error log" --label "error-summary"
```
</examples>

    # Accepted narrow risk (review 2026-07-22): same name + identical prompt

"""Superset Claude agent-status notify hook.

Installed by agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts. POSTs each Claude lifecycle
event to the host-service (SUPERSET_HOST_AGENT_HOOK_URL) so the agent-status
dots are driven event-driven — reviving what the dead bash notify.sh did.

Event -> eventType mapping (NEVER defaults to Stop on an unknown event; an
unmapped event is a silent no-op, exactly like notify.sh):
  UserPromptSubmit            -> Start            (working / yellow)
  Stop                        -> Stop             (review/green) UNLESS a
                                 subagent is still running (then suppressed —
                                 stay yellow; greens on the last SubagentStop).
                                 With background_tasks[] still running, the
                                 entry TYPES decide: any agent-type entry
                                 (subagent/teammate/workflow) -> SubagentActive
                                 (yellow; red-respecting in the renderer);
                                 shell-only -> BackgroundRunning (blue)
  SessionEnd                  -> Stop             (review / green; clears state)
  StopFailure(main loop)      -> Stop + clears state, UNLESS a codex-companion
                                 job for this session is still alive ->
                                 SubagentActive (BF: codex runs on its OWN API;
                                 a Claude rate-limit abort does not stop it)
  StopFailure(in a subagent)  -> (STOPFAIL-SUBAGENT) self-scoped: drops only that
                                 fork's markers, never the shared session state /
                                 the main question guard; the central red guard
                                 keeps a still-pending AskUserQuestion red
  Notification                -> PermissionRequest (permission / red)
  PreToolUse(AskUserQuestion) -> PermissionRequest (red)   else no-op
  PostToolUse(main loop)      -> Start             (working — clears red after
                                 a permission approval or an answered question:
                                 the main loop is sequential, so a completed
                                 main-loop tool proves the red was handled)
  PostToolUse(in a subagent)  -> SubagentActive    ((SUBTOOL-RED) payload carries
                                 agent_id ONLY for tool calls inside a subagent;
                                 background agents' completions stream in WHILE
                                 an AskUserQuestion/permission red is pending and
                                 must assert working WITHOUT clearing that red)
  PostToolUseFailure          -> aliased to PostToolUse (a failed tool is the same

content.content:
1	## Verdict: REFUTED
2	
3	The `TaskStop` ledger omission is real, but it did not cause this stuck yellow. The actual cause was Windows CP1252 decoding corrupting UTF-8 hook input, which broke teammate prompt-prefix matching.
4	
5	### Primary session evidence
6	
7	- The transcript confirms `outlook-atif2` was spawned, stopped, and never idle-notified:
8	
9	  - Line 128: spawn with the Care Vision prompt.
10	  - Line 146: `TaskStop {"task_id":"outlook-atif2"}`.
11	  - Line 147: successful result for internal task `tj791ti5t`, `task_type="in_process_teammate"`.
12	  - The teamstate consequently retains `outlook-atif2="active"`.
13	
14	- However, [agent-notify-hook.log](/C:/Users/khair/.superset/agent-notify-hook.log:508058) shows:
15	
16	  - Line 508058, before the stop: `tj791ti5t` is present and its description correctly prefix-matches `outlook-atif2`.
17	  - Line 508149: successful `PostToolUse:TaskStop`.
18	  - Line 508151: the next background snapshot no longer contains `tj791ti5t`.
19	  - Final line 509428 contains only five other teammate entries.
20	
21	So the harness did not retain the stopped Care Vision task forever; it removed it immediately.
22	
23	Replaying `_team_entry_droppable` against that final five-entry payload gives:
24	
25	| Raw task | Ledger match | Result |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| `t2qwrubdp` | `outlook-atif=idle` | dropped |
28	| Three research IDs | three research teammates, all idle | dropped |
29	| `t1ryk141d` | no match | kept |
30	
31	`t1ryk141d` is `draft-labelid`. Its payload description contains:
32	
33	```text
34	Create an Outlook DRAFT (never send â€” the script h...
35	```
36	
37	The stored prompt contains a real em dash, `—` (U+2014). The payload contains the mojibake sequence `â€”` (U+00E2 U+20AC U+201D). Therefore `p.startswith(prefix)` fails and the fail-safe matcher keeps the entry even though `draft-labelid="idle"`.
38	
39	The encoding boundary is conclusive:
40	
41	- [pane-map-hook.ts](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:434>) read hook JSON with text-mode `sys.stdin.read()`.
42	- `uv run python` in this environment reports:
43	
44	```text
45	stdin=cp1252
46	preferred=cp1252
47	utf8_mode=0
48	```
49	
50	- The transcript is explicitly read as UTF-8, so only the hook payload side is corrupted.
51	
52	### Why `agents=[...]` looked contradictory
53	
54	It is a raw-ID list, not the effective kept list:
55	
56	- [pane-map-hook.ts](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:1925>) filters into `bg_tasks_eff`.
57	- `bg_ids` deliberately comes from the raw payload for marker reconciliation.
58	- The Stop reason logs raw `bg_ids` whenever any effective entry remains.
59	
60	Thus `agents=['t1ryk...', ...]` means “five raw running IDs”; it does not mean all five survived filtering. The absence of `tj791ti5t` positively shows that Care Vision was no longer involved.
61	
62	All five had `status="running"`, so `_bg_entry_finished` correctly treated them as unfinished. Four were then dropped by ledger matching, leaving the mojibake-corrupted draft entry.
63	
64	## Alternatives eliminated
65	
66	- Per-subagent run directory: empty.
67	- `.askq`: empty.
68	- No `.mainstopped`, `.compacting`, or `.shellbg`.
69	- Codex companion: zero matching records for session `6df86412-...` among 239 job files inspected.
70	- `.agentbg` was derived from the same faulty effective background list, not an independent cause.
71	- `.bgactive` was only approximately 11 seconds old at the final Stop, so the 900-second stale reap correctly did not activate. Aging does not autonomously emit green; another hook event is required.
72	- Renderer behavior is correct. [statusTransitions.ts](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/renderer/routes/_authenticated/components/V2NotificationController/lib/statusTransitions.ts:64>) makes `SubagentActive` set working, while a later turn-end clears working. [store.ts](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/renderer/stores/v2-notifications/store.ts:73>) derives permission > working > review and persists the axes through renderer reloads.
73	- [agent-dot-render.log](/C:/Users/khair/.superset/agent-dot-render.log:1301) confirms the terminal remained `working`; it was not merely a visual folding error.
74	- A stale shell axis cannot produce yellow and is gated off for registered agent terminals.
75	
76	Consequently, “poisoned until teamstate deletion or transcript change” is too absolute. A later Stop after `.bgactive` becomes stale, SessionEnd/StopFailure, detach/close/interrupt, or a full app restart can clear the visible yellow.
77	
78	## Second session
79	
80	Terminal `9ab87b09-...`, session `fc8dbc86-...`, is not a TaskStop case: its entire transcript contains no `TaskStop`.
81	
82	At the requested `kept 4` snapshot, [agent-notify-hook.log](/C:/Users/khair/.superset/agent-notify-hook.log:506646) contains six raw entries:
83	
84	- Two clean `You are investigating...` prefixes matched idle names and were dropped.
85	- Three prefixes contained the same `â€”` corruption and falsely failed matching.
86	- `sol-final` had genuinely spawned about eight seconds earlier and was active.
87	
88	Therefore:
89	
90	- Same actual encoding defect: yes, for three false keeps.
91	- Same proposed TaskStop class: no.
92	- Yellow was still legitimate at that exact snapshot because one teammate was genuinely active.
93	
94	## Minimal proposed fix
95	
96	The fix belongs at the API boundary, not in `_team_norm`, and should use strict UTF-8 rather than replacement decoding:
97	
98	```diff
99	diff --git a/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts b/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts
100	--- a/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts
101	+++ b/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts
102	@@
103	 def _read_payload():
104	     candidates = []
105	     try:
106	-        raw = sys.stdin.read()
107	+        stream = getattr(sys.stdin, "buffer", None)
108	+        raw = (
109	+            stream.read().decode("utf-8")
110	+            if stream is not None
111	+            else sys.stdin.read()
112	+        )
113	         if raw:
114	             candidates.append(raw)
115	-    except (OSError, ValueError):
116	-        pass
117	+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
118	+        _log({
119	+            "action": "payload-read-error",
120	+            "error": str(exc),
121	+            "stdinEncoding": getattr(sys.stdin, "encoding", None),
122	+        })
123	```
124	
125	I would not use `decode("utf-8", "replace")`: that hides malformed input and can create another silent prefix mismatch. Strict decoding plus explicit logging fails loud without aborting Claude’s hook runner.
126	
127	The durable change must be in the embedded `NOTIFY_SCRIPT`. [writeNotifyScriptIfChanged](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:2205>) compares and rewrites `C:\Users\khair\.superset\hooks\superset-notify.py`; [installPaneMapHook](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:2407>) runs when the desktop watcher starts. Thus a rebuilt desktop main-process restart materializes the fix. Editing only the live script is temporary.
128	
129	### TaskStop hardening critique
130	
131	TaskStop support remains worthwhile ledger hygiene, but it would not fix this incident.
132	
133	Safe behavior should:
134	
135	- Never mark idle from the `tool_use` alone; failed TaskStops exist.
136	- Persist `tool_use_id -> requested task_id`, then require the paired successful result.
137	- Require `task_type=="in_process_teammate"` and a success result.
138	- Resolve a known bare name first, then `name@team` only when its base is known.
139	- For internal `t...` IDs, use the result’s command prefix only if it uniquely identifies one stored prompt.
140	- On zero or multiple matches, retain active and log ambiguity.
141	- Bump teamstate schema v3→v4 so old transcripts containing TaskStops are rescanned.
142	- Leave existing `SendMessage -> active` semantics: current Claude documentation confirms that messaging a stopped subagent resumes it automatically. [Claude Code tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference)

## Verdict: REFUTED

The `TaskStop` ledger omission is real, but it did not cause this stuck yellow. The actual cause was Windows CP1252 decoding corrupting UTF-8 hook input, which broke teammate prompt-prefix matching.

### Primary session evidence

- The transcript confirms `outlook-atif2` was spawned, stopped, and never idle-notified:

  - Line 128: spawn with the Care Vision prompt.
  - Line 146: `TaskStop {"task_id":"outlook-atif2"}`.
  - Line 147: successful result for internal task `tj791ti5t`, `task_type="in_process_teammate"`.
  - The teamstate consequently retains `outlook-atif2="active"`.

- However, [agent-notify-hook.log](/C:/Users/khair/.superset/agent-notify-hook.log:508058) shows:

  - Line 508058, before the stop: `tj791ti5t` is present and its description correctly prefix-matches `outlook-atif2`.
  - Line 508149: successful `PostToolUse:TaskStop`.
  - Line 508151: the next background snapshot no longer contains `tj791ti5t`.
  - Final line 509428 contains only five other teammate entries.

So the harness did not retain the stopped Care Vision task forever; it removed it immediately.

Replaying `_team_entry_droppable` against that final five-entry payload gives:

| Raw task | Ledger match | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `t2qwrubdp` | `outlook-atif=idle` | dropped |
| Three research IDs | three research teammates, all idle | dropped |
| `t1ryk141d` | no match | kept |

`t1ryk141d` is `draft-labelid`. Its payload description contains:

```text
Create an Outlook DRAFT (never send â€” the script h...
```

The stored prompt contains a real em dash, `—` (U+2014). The payload contains the mojibake sequence `â€”` (U+00E2 U+20AC U+201D). Therefore `p.startswith(prefix)` fails and the fail-safe matcher keeps the entry even though `draft-labelid="idle"`.

The encoding boundary is conclusive:

- [pane-map-hook.ts](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:434>) read hook JSON with text-mode `sys.stdin.read()`.
- `uv run python` in this environment reports:

```text
stdin=cp1252
preferred=cp1252
utf8_mode=0
```

- The transcript is explicitly read as UTF-8, so only the hook payload side is corrupted.

### Why `agents=[...]` looked contradictory

It is a raw-ID list, not the effective kept list:

- [pane-map-hook.ts](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:1925>) filters into `bg_tasks_eff`.
- `bg_ids` deliberately comes from the raw payload for marker reconciliation.
- The Stop reason logs raw `bg_ids` whenever any effective entry remains.

Thus `agents=['t1ryk...', ...]` means “five raw running IDs”; it does not mean all five survived filtering. The absence of `tj791ti5t` positively shows that Care Vision was no longer involved.

All five had `status="running"`, so `_bg_entry_finished` correctly treated them as unfinished. Four were then dropped by ledger matching, leaving the mojibake-corrupted draft entry.

## Alternatives eliminated

- Per-subagent run directory: empty.
- `.askq`: empty.
- No `.mainstopped`, `.compacting`, or `.shellbg`.
- Codex companion: zero matching records for session `6df86412-...` among 239 job files inspected.
- `.agentbg` was derived from the same faulty effective background list, not an independent cause.
- `.bgactive` was only approximately 11 seconds old at the final Stop, so the 900-second stale reap correctly did not activate. Aging does not autonomously emit green; another hook event is required.
- Renderer behavior is correct. [statusTransitions.ts](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/renderer/routes/_authenticated/components/V2NotificationController/lib/statusTransitions.ts:64>) makes `SubagentActive` set working, while a later turn-end clears working. [store.ts](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/renderer/stores/v2-notifications/store.ts:73>) derives permission > working > review and persists the axes through renderer reloads.
- [agent-dot-render.log](/C:/Users/khair/.superset/agent-dot-render.log:1301) confirms the terminal remained `working`; it was not merely a visual folding error.
- A stale shell axis cannot produce yellow and is gated off for registered agent terminals.

Consequently, “poisoned until teamstate deletion or transcript change” is too absolute. A later Stop after `.bgactive` becomes stale, SessionEnd/StopFailure, detach/close/interrupt, or a full app restart can clear the visible yellow.

## Second session

Terminal `9ab87b09-...`, session `fc8dbc86-...`, is not a TaskStop case: its entire transcript contains no `TaskStop`.

At the requested `kept 4` snapshot, [agent-notify-hook.log](/C:/Users/khair/.superset/agent-notify-hook.log:506646) contains six raw entries:

- Two clean `You are investigating...` prefixes matched idle names and were dropped.
- Three prefixes contained the same `â€”` corruption and falsely failed matching.
- `sol-final` had genuinely spawned about eight seconds earlier and was active.

Therefore:

- Same actual encoding defect: yes, for three false keeps.
- Same proposed TaskStop class: no.
- Yellow was still legitimate at that exact snapshot because one teammate was genuinely active.

## Minimal proposed fix

The fix belongs at the API boundary, not in `_team_norm`, and should use strict UTF-8 rather than replacement decoding:

```diff
diff --git a/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts b/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts
--- a/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts
+++ b/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts
@@
 def _read_payload():
     candidates = []
     try:
-        raw = sys.stdin.read()
+        stream = getattr(sys.stdin, "buffer", None)
+        raw = (
+            stream.read().decode("utf-8")
+            if stream is not None
+            else sys.stdin.read()
+        )
         if raw:
             candidates.append(raw)
-    except (OSError, ValueError):
-        pass
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        _log({
+            "action": "payload-read-error",
+            "error": str(exc),
+            "stdinEncoding": getattr(sys.stdin, "encoding", None),
+        })
```

I would not use `decode("utf-8", "replace")`: that hides malformed input and can create another silent prefix mismatch. Strict decoding plus explicit logging fails loud without aborting Claude’s hook runner.

The durable change must be in the embedded `NOTIFY_SCRIPT`. [writeNotifyScriptIfChanged](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:2205>) compares and rewrites `C:\Users\khair\.superset\hooks\superset-notify.py`; [installPaneMapHook](</C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:2407>) runs when the desktop watcher starts. Thus a rebuilt desktop main-process restart materializes the fix. Editing only the live script is temporary.

### TaskStop hardening critique

TaskStop support remains worthwhile ledger hygiene, but it would not fix this incident.

Safe behavior should:

- Never mark idle from the `tool_use` alone; failed TaskStops exist.
- Persist `tool_use_id -> requested task_id`, then require the paired successful result.
- Require `task_type=="in_process_teammate"` and a success result.
- Resolve a known bare name first, then `name@team` only when its base is known.
- For internal `t...` IDs, use the result’s command prefix only if it uniquely identifies one stored prompt.
- On zero or multiple matches, retain active and log ambiguity.
- Bump teamstate schema v3→v4 so old transcripts containing TaskStops are rescanned.
- Leave existing `SendMessage -> active` semantics: current Claude documentation confirms that messaging a stopped subagent resumes it automatically. [Claude Code tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference)

TEAM-ENTRY-MATCH missed this because it was designed to isolate unrelated poisoned names, not invent missing termination events. Its source comment explicitly leaves “died without reporting” entries to BG-STALE. In this incident it worked: stale `outlook-atif2=active` did not poison the other entries.

Other unledgered termination paths include teammate crash/API abort without idle, natural completion whose idle message never reaches an already-ended lead session, and non-fork completion without an idle notification. Current Claude also exposes a direct `TeammateIdle` hook, which would be a cleaner future signal than transcript inference. [Claude Code hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)

## Proposed logging

For every kept teammate entry, log a bounded record containing:

- Raw task ID, type, and status.
- Escaped normalized prefix or a hash plus a short redacted preview.
- Matching teammate names and current states.
- Explicit keep reason: `short-prefix`, `unmatched`, `ambiguous`, or `matched-active`.
- Separate `rawAgentIds` and `effectiveKeptAgentIds`.

Also:

- Log UTF-8 decode failures with byte count, error offset, and `sys.stdin.encoding`, without logging payload contents.
- Add renderer axes (`permission`, `working`, `review`) to render snapshots, not only the derived colour.
- Do not dump full prompts or the entire ledger: these can contain email content, paths, or PHI.

Finally, the workspace changed concurrently during this read-only investigation: initial status had only the pre-existing `.playwright-mcp/`; it now shows an uncommitted modification to `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.ts`, and the live hook changed at 00:36. I did not create, modify, revert, or commit those changes.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Superset pane-map SessionStart hook (v1).

Installed by agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts. Writes a
{paneId, tabId, workspaceId} record keyed by the agent session id
so the watcher can resolve per-pane identity beyond cwd matching.

Logging: every invocation appends one JSON line to
~/.superset/pane-map-hook.log (gate with SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG=0).
The logger can never raise — a broken hook must not abort the agent.
"""
import datetime
import json
import os
import pathlib
import sys


def _log(record: dict) -> None:
    # Append one JSON line to ~/.superset/pane-map-hook.log. Fully
    # self-contained and never raises: any failure (disk, perms,
    # serialization) is swallowed so the hook can never break the agent.
    if os.environ.get("SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG") == "0":
        return
    try:
        record["ts"] = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()
        record["phase"] = "hook"
        log_dir = pathlib.Path.home() / ".superset"
        log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        log_path = log_dir / "pane-map-hook.log"
        with open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


def _read_payload():
    # Codex passes the hook payload as argv[1]; Claude/Mastra/Droid
    # pipe via stdin. Try both. Returns (payload_or_None, source,
    # skip_reason). source is "argv[1]" | "stdin" | "none". skip_reason
    # distinguishes invalid-payload-json vs payload-not-object for the
    # diagnostic log; main() decides whether to abort.
    stdin_bytes = 0
    candidates = []
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        candidates.append(("argv[1]", sys.argv[1]))
    try:
        raw = sys.stdin.read()
        if raw:
            stdin_bytes = len(raw.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
            candidates.append(("stdin", raw))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    if not candidates:
        return None, "none", "none", stdin_bytes
    saw_parse_error = False
    for source, src in candidates:
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(src)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            saw_parse_error = True
            continue
        if isinstance(parsed, dict):
            return parsed, source, None, stdin_bytes
        return None, source, "payload-not-object", stdin_bytes
    return None, candidates[0][0], "invalid-payload-json" if saw_parse_error else "none", stdin_bytes


def main() -> None:
    pid = os.getpid()
    argv_count = len(sys.argv)
    superset_env = {
        "SUPERSET_PANE_ID": os.environ.get("SUPERSET_PANE_ID", ""),
        "SUPERSET_TAB_ID": os.environ.get("SUPERSET_TAB_ID", ""),
        "SUPERSET_TERMINAL_ID": os.environ.get("SUPERSET_TERMINAL_ID", ""),
        "SUPERSET_WORKSPACE_ID": os.environ.get("SUPERSET_WORKSPACE_ID", ""),
    }

    # Read both v1 and v2 terminal-identity env vars. At least one of
    # pane_id (v1) or terminal_id (v2) must be present to indicate this
    # is a Superset-launched terminal.
    pane_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_PANE_ID", "").strip()
    tab_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_TAB_ID", "").strip()
    terminal_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_TERMINAL_ID", "").strip()
    workspace_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_WORKSPACE_ID", "").strip()
    if not pane_id and not terminal_id:
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": 0,
            "payloadSource": "none",
            "payloadKeys": [],
            "rawSessionIdFields": {},
            "sessionId": None,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": None,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": "missing-terminal-env",
            "outPath": None,
            "error": None,
        })
        return  # not inside a Superset-launched terminal

    payload, payload_source, payload_skip, stdin_bytes = _read_payload()
    payload_dict = payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
    payload_keys = sorted(payload_dict.keys())
    raw_session_id_fields = {
        "session_id": payload_dict.get("session_id"),
        "sessionId": payload_dict.get("sessionId"),
        "resourceId": payload_dict.get("resourceId"),
        "resource_id": payload_dict.get("resource_id"),
    }
    if payload_skip in ("invalid-payload-json", "payload-not-object"):
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
            "payloadSource": payload_source,
            "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
            "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
            "sessionId": None,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": None,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": payload_skip,
            "outPath": None,
            "error": None,
        })
        return

    session_id = (
        payload_dict.get("session_id")
        or payload_dict.get("sessionId")
        or payload_dict.get("resourceId")
        or payload_dict.get("resource_id")
    )
    if not session_id or not isinstance(session_id, str):
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
            "payloadSource": payload_source,
            "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
            "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
            "sessionId": session_id if isinstance(session_id, str) else None,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": None,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": "missing-session-id",
            "outPath": None,
            "error": None,
        })
        return

    # Only emit fields that have values — keeps the mapping file
    # minimal and lets the watcher's spread skip undefined fields.
    mapping: dict = {}
    if pane_id:
        mapping["paneId"] = pane_id
    if tab_id:
        mapping["tabId"] = tab_id
    if terminal_id:
        mapping["terminalId"] = terminal_id
    if workspace_id:
        mapping["workspaceId"] = workspace_id

    out_dir = pathlib.Path.home() / ".superset" / "session-pane-map"
    try:
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    except OSError as exc:
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
            "payloadSource": payload_source,
            "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
            "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
            "sessionId": session_id,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": mapping,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": "mkdir-failed",
            "outPath": None,
            "error": str(exc),
        })
        return
    out_path = out_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
    try:
        out_path.write_text(
            json.dumps(mapping),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    except OSError as exc:
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
            "payloadSource": payload_source,
            "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
            "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
            "sessionId": session_id,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": mapping,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": "write-failed",
            "outPath": str(out_path),
            "error": str(exc),
        })
        return

    _log({
